title: $1000 off Chery Tiggo 4 or $1000 Fuel Card (from $23,990 Driveaway Before Discount) @ Chery
body:
Deal: $1000 off Chery Tiggo 4 or $1000 Fuel Card (from $23,990 Driveaway Before Discount) @ Chery

[Mortgagetightass] Everyone will knock these, and yes they're very average cars to drive.
But reddit/ozb make up a very small percentage of customers who are after a nice driving/dynamic rear wheel drive.
22k driveaway with 10-year warranty, cheap servicing and low risk of depreciation given the very low entry price.
cheap, cheerful motoring.. there's a reason these have sold 45,000+ units in 4 years in Australia (given the SUV boom)
What's comparable at this size from a legacy brand? A Honda HRV? with only 4 seats at $34,000? with less warranty?
Or a RAV4 which is a better car no doubt, but you can almost buy 3 of these for the same money. Toyota has half the warranty too…
this is good for Tom, Dick, Jane and even Rajesh to get around town with decent tech and fuel economy.
[thatguyfromthatplace] Cheap financing too because it's new rather than used. If all you're doing is pootling about in the suburbs then it's kinda perfect.
[Nom] Why did you only quote half the sentence ?
The important part that you missed, is given the very low entry price.
It's so cheap that even when it depreciates 50% then you've only lost 12 grand.
[CheapandUsed] This is perfect for the target market that the Mitsubishi ASX abandoned when they decided to retire the ancient previous model and replace it with the incredibly expensive Renault Captur model share.
Chery even include a call out to the 'diamond shape grille' in the marketing to really hammer it home… Mitsubishi have long linked their diamond shape logo to their marketing (e.g. Mitsubishi Diamond Advantage)
[Brick Tamland] ASX gets better fuel economy despite being ancient. Will be more reliable. Nicer to drive. And you can get a fairly recent model with low KM for about the same price or less.

My father 25 years old Camery Touring V6 Station wagon was almost 40K before on road cost. An OZBs believe Toyota should sell a 2026 RAV4 at almost half that price?

Would like to hear what owners are getting?

We know you're addicted to hating Chinese car deals but try using your brain before you press post 😂
[Brick Tamland] @shxhshzhz: What will really blow your mind is my 2.0l turbo that puts out 221KW is officially rated as the same fuel economy. How on earth can a car with half the power use the same amount of petrol through a smaller and non-turbo engine. Mind blowing.
[shxhshzhz] @Brick Tamland: What will blow your mind is that your 2.0L turbo car costs nowhere near $22,990 brand new and isn't comparable or relevant to this deal in any way
[Brick Tamland] @shxhshzhz: I am comparing the fuel use and the level of engineering that is absent in these cheap Chinese cars. The world has moved on from fuel guzzling cars.

How can it be so high or are these heavier vehicles with a 1.5l pushing daisies?

also i dont have to get up for old farts ndis folks or unfortuanate preganate types
[eddyah] touch some grass loser.
most people have no issues catching public transport and are trying to get by without being judged
[Jackson] Steer clear of these unless you are going for an EV, much less chance of things going wrong. Even when things don't go wrong. I have been in one of these and even when you are wringing it's neck it's going nowhere
You can get EVs for this price now, albeit second hand but still with some warranty, which will be better than this in every way and a much, much less risky proposition, and cost you much less to run
[EtherealArchelon] Had one recently as a rental.
First 15 minutes were terrifying when it tried to push me into a road train with its Lane assist while it was raining.
It also beeped at me for yawning.
I like the fact I never had to get my keys out of my bag because it automatically unlocked and locked the car based on proximity. I assume this is quite common in new cars but I've never had it before.
10 days of <20mins driving a day was $30 in fuel
[NotReallyaMoneySaver] It's $15.50 cents for 8L/100Km, using E10. So you're driving total 200Km 3.33 hrs (200 minutes) of driving = 1 km/m i.e. 60Km/h avg. So you were driving at minimum speed 60km/hr?
[HoLeeFuk] I've had the Chery Tiggo 4 for three weeks, and these are the issues I've experienced: servicing is fully booked everywhere, so you need to book about a month in advance. Fuel economy is around 9 L/100 km in city driving and 8 L/100 km on the freeway. The head unit is also a bit unstable and keeps disconnecting from Android Auto. Other than that, it's a beautiful car to drive, especially for the price.
[Mokr] Fuel economy is around 9 L/100 km in city driving and 8 L/100 km on the freeway.
Normal fuel economy for city driving, but bad for freeway.
[goodwillN1] I drive a 2015 2.0L Turbo with a little over 8 litres/100km average in the city. 9 litres for a small SUV with smaller engine is NOT normal. It is on the worse end. Plenty of newer small cars should be able to do 7-8 in city and around 6 on freeway.
